text:
A: Hi, can you hear me okay? Great. I'm Gemma, I'm in Hornchurch.
B: Tracey. Sittingbourne.
A: Oh, Kent, not too far then. So what do you do?
B: Replenishment at a supermarket. Shelf stacking. Early mornings, start at five.
A: Five! Gosh. I'm a speech and language therapist. Self-employed now, mostly after-school clients and a Saturday morning. Before that I did about ten years in NHS community paediatrics, so, you know, I know the system inside out.
B: Right. So kids that can't talk properly?
A: Well, sort of. It's more speech sound delays, language delays, kids who are behind with putting sentences together. It's not just "can't talk", yeah?
B: My sister's youngest had something like that. Waited about a year on the NHS.
A: Yeah, that's the problem, the waiting lists are shocking. That's partly why people come private.
B: Couldn't afford private, to be honest.
A: No, I get that, it isn't cheap. Erm, so do you like the early shifts?
B: Love finishing at eleven. Rest of the day's mine. Getting up at quarter past four's the killer.
A: I'd be knackered. I'm out at parkrun Saturdays if I haven't got clients, and even that feels early.
B: Running for fun? No thanks. I walk the dog round the rec, that'll do me.
A: What have you got?
B: Staffie. Roxy. She's old now, dodgy hips. The vet bills are something else.
A: Oh bless her. My son Alfie's desperate for a dog, but Dean says absolutely not.
B: My other half's Dean.
A: No way! What does yours do?
B: Scaffolder. Self-employed.
A: Mine's an electrician, got his own little business. He leaves the van on the drive at this ridiculous angle every single night and it drives me up the wall, I've told him a hundred times.
B: That's every bloke with a van. Ours broke down again last week, I had to go and fetch him from Faversham.
A: Oh, nightmare. Did you get on alright with that puzzle at the start, by the way?
B: Gave up halfway. Couldn't be bothered.
A: I finished it with about a minute to spare, actually.
B: Course you did.
A: Sorry, what's that supposed to mean?
B: Nothing bad. You just look organised. I saw that calendar behind you with all the colours.
A: Okay, guilty. It's colour-coded by child. Ruby's just started secondary and the homework's ridiculous, so I have to track it or we'd fall apart.
B: Mine's a free one from the Chinese. Says Lucky Garden on it.
A: Ha. Is that your Friday night then?
B: Every Friday. Chicken chow mein, salt and pepper chips. Not changing that.
A: We're a curry family on a Friday. Dean'd riot if I tried to cook.
B: Same. Fridays I'm not doing nothing.
